newsitem.title: THAILAND: RESEARCH ALERT-Bangkok Bank rated buy.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT-Bangkok Bank rated buy.

text.p: Socgen-Crosby Research Ltd recommended on Wednesday that investors buy stocks of Bangkok Bank Plc due to the bank's high asset quality and ability to control operating expenses.
"With consistent credit growth and stringent controls, BBL remains our top pick in terms of asset quality," Socgen-Crosby said in a new report.
The research house expects further declines in Bangkok Bank's operating costs due to the bank's greater use of automation as well as a cost containment policy.

Socgen-Crosby said Bangkok Bank's first-quarter net profit of 5.03 billion baht ($193.5 million) was in line with its projection and expected the bank to post a net profit of 21.93 billion baht for the whole of 1997.
In 1996, Bangkok Bank, Thailand's largest commercial bank, announced a profit of 20.75 billion baht compared with 19.70 billion in the previous year.

Bangkok Bank's loan growth in 1997 is likely to be between eight to 10 percent compared with a rise of 8.4 percent a year ago due to the sluggish economy and some delay in key infrastructure projects, it said.
"While the Thai economy hasn't fully recovered, we do expect both loan and deposit growth to pick up along with the recovery, however, slight it may be," Socgen-Crosby said.
